chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Muskan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a pigeon that was slaughtered in the al-Hill (non-sanctuary state)

He said: 'The Muhrim (one in Ihram) does not eat it. And if it was brought to Mecca, the Muhill (one who ends Ihram) eats it in Mecca. And if it was brought to the Haram (sanctuary) alive, then slaughtered in the Haram, he should not eat it, because it was slaughtered after it had reached its place of safety (from the effects of Ihram).'

key_terms.اَلْحِلُّ: The non-sanctuary state, opposite of Haram
key_terms.مَأْمَنَهُ: Its place of safety/security (from Ihram restrictions)
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One who has ended the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for eating birds slaughtered by a pilgrim in Ihram inside or outside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific juristic distinction regarding the consumption of game slaughtered by a pilgrim, emphasizing that the prohibition persists until the animal reaches its 'place of safety' (*Ma'manah*). It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the precise timing of when the state of Ihram's restrictions lift, differentiating between slaughter in the open country (*Hill*) versus within the sacred precincts (*Haram*).
